en.name: Peanuts in the shell
en.summary: Peanuts in the shell keep 4 months from purchase in a cool, dry cupboard — several times longer than shelled ones — and 12 months in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, or 24 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F).
en.pantry: 4 months from purchase, cool, dark and above all dry, ideally in a mesh bag or an open basket rather than sealed plastic. The shell is a genuine barrier: it keeps most of the oxygen away from the kernel, which is why in-shell peanuts get months at room temperature where shelled ones get weeks. Humidity is the thing to guard against, because a damp shell is where mould starts, and warm damp storage is the classic way to ruin a sack of peanuts.
en.fridge: 12 months from purchase at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. The shell buys a lot, but cold buys more, and it is worth the shelf space for anything you have bought in quantity. Keep them in a paper bag or a loosely closed box rather than a sealed plastic one — sealed plastic traps the moisture that the shells give off, and that is the one condition you do not want.
en.freezer: 24 months from purchase at −18 °C (0 °F). In-shell peanuts freeze perfectly well because there is almost no free water in the kernel. They are bulky, so shell them first if freezer space is tight; the shelled figure is the same 24 months. Bag them airtight and let the bag return to room temperature sealed before opening.
en.thawing: No thawing required. Bring the sealed bag back to room temperature before opening it, so that condensation forms on the bag and not on the shells.
spoilage: Shells that are blackened, stained or visibly mouldy.
A musty, damp-cellar smell when you crack a handful open.
Shrivelled, discoloured or bitter kernels inside sound-looking shells.
Kernels that rattle loose and taste of old oil.
tips: Store in mesh or paper, not sealed plastic; shells need to breathe.
Crack a few from different parts of the bag before serving a bowlful.
Shell them before freezing if space is tight — the timeline is the same either way.
Discard the whole bag if it smells musty rather than sorting the good from the bad.

faq.q: How long do peanuts in the shell keep?
faq.a: 4 months from purchase in a cool, dry cupboard, 12 months in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, or 24 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F).

faq.q: Why do in-shell peanuts last longer than shelled ones?
faq.a: The shell keeps oxygen off the kernel, and it is oxidation of the oil that makes peanuts rancid. Shelled peanuts get weeks in a cupboard; in-shell ones get months.

faq.q: How can you tell if peanuts in the shell have gone bad?
faq.a: Crack a few open. Musty smells, stained shells or shrivelled, bitter kernels mean the bag goes.

zh.name: 帶殼花生
zh.summary: 帶殼花生自購買日起，放在陰涼乾燥的櫥櫃可放 4 個月——是去殼花生的好幾倍；4 °C 以下冷藏 12 個月，−18 °C 冷凍 24 個月。
zh.pantry: 陰涼、避光，最重要的是乾燥，自購買日起 4 個月；用網袋或敞口籃子比密封塑膠袋好。殼是真正的屏障，它把大部分氧氣擋在果仁之外，這就是為什麼帶殼的以「月」計、去殼的只以「週」計。要防的是濕氣，因為霉就是從潮濕的殼開始長的，而又熱又濕的存放正是毀掉一整袋花生的經典方式。
zh.fridge: 放 4 °C 以下，自購買日起 12 個月。殼幫了很多忙，低溫幫得更多；量買得多的話，值得占這個位子。請用紙袋或蓋不緊的盒子，不要用密封塑膠盒——密封會把殼散出的水氣困住，而那正是你最不想要的狀況。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下，自購買日起 24 個月。帶殼花生非常耐凍，因為果仁裡幾乎沒有自由水。它很占空間，冷凍庫緊的話可以先剝殼再凍，去殼的期限同樣是 24 個月。請密封裝袋，並且維持密封回到室溫再打開。
zh.thawing: 不需要解凍。請讓密封袋回到室溫再打開，讓結露留在袋子上而不是殼上。
spoilage: 殼發黑、有污斑，或看得到霉。
剝開一把時聞到潮濕地窖般的霉味。
外觀正常的殼裡面，果仁乾癟、變色或發苦。
果仁在殼裡鬆動作響，吃起來有久放的油味。
tips: 用網袋或紙袋，不要密封塑膠；殼需要透氣。
整盤端出去之前，先從袋子不同位置剝幾顆檢查。
冷凍庫空間不夠就先剝殼再凍，期限一樣。
整袋有霉味就整袋丟，不要挑好的留下。

faq.a: 自購買日起，放陰涼乾燥的櫥櫃 4 個月，4 °C 以下冷藏 12 個月，−18 °C 冷凍 24 個月。

faq.q: 為什麼帶殼花生比去殼的耐放？
faq.a: 殼把氧氣擋在果仁外，而讓花生油耗的正是油脂氧化。去殼的在櫥櫃裡以週計，帶殼的以月計。

faq.q: 怎麼判斷帶殼花生壞了？
faq.a: 剝幾顆來看。有霉味、殼上有污斑，或果仁乾癟發苦，整袋就該丟。
